author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: An AI search engine that answers questions directly instead of listing links.
what_it_does: Perplexity answers a question with a written response and citations rather than a page of blue links. It sells a paid tier with better models and has pushed into shopping and a browser.
how_it_makes_money: Consumer subscriptions, a developer interface, and advertising and commerce experiments. Subscriptions dominate.
why_it_matters: It is the most direct commercial attack on web search, and the clearest test of whether AI answers can be a business rather than a feature.
competitive_position: Competes with Google, which can copy any feature instantly and distribute it to billions, and with ChatGPT's own search. It has to be meaningfully better to survive.
key_risks: Its main competitor owns the distribution channel and the default position on most devices.
Publishers have objected to content use, creating legal and licensing exposure.
Model costs sit directly against subscription revenue, compressing margin.
Consumer subscriptions churn more easily than enterprise contracts.

glossary.definition: A search product that returns a written answer with sources rather than a ranked list of pages.
